summary: The prepared base already contains the #32467 removal of the racing warp-scratch initialization. Added focused GPU regression coverage for the reported ragged shapes and independent reduction boundaries; no production source change was justified.

tests.what_was_measured: Real GPU-input plan_prefill kernel output for the two reported ragged shapes, a uniform control, and partial-warp/full-block/zero-extend boundaries; 3 tests passed.
Adjacent DSV4 CPU/GPU planner invariants; 5 tests and 82 subtests passed.

tests.what_was_measured: 9,000 gfx950 kernel launches; zero out-of-bounds ragged plans, with exact maximum ragged IDs 383 for 384 rows and 359 for both 360-row reported ragged inputs.

tests.command: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .../python < direct repeated planner harness with historical five-line initialization temporarily restored
tests.what_was_measured: Local failing-before attempt on gfx950; zero bad plans in 4,000 ragged launches, so the timing-sensitive historical NVIDIA failure was not reproduced on the assigned AMD GPU.

gpu_evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / ROCm 7.2.26015; raw logs under /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-97a7771a49e3/evidence/.
remaining_limitations: Assigned hardware was one gfx950 GPU, not NVIDIA B300 TP8; TP8, CUDA Graph replay, NCCL, and cross-rank behavior remain unverified locally.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark weights were unavailable, so no full-model or semantic accuracy reproduction was performed.
Temporarily restoring the historical racing initialization did not reproduce the timing-sensitive failure on gfx950; failing-before evidence remains platform-specific upstream evidence.
